note: Advisories that check-npm-audit.mjs must not fail on. Only add an entry when NO published version resolves the advisory — if a newer pin fixes it, raise the pin in TemplateVersions.kt instead. Entries are keyed by GHSA id, never by package name, so a future unrelated vulnerability in the same package still fails the gate. Every entry needs a reason, a url, a reviewed date, and an expires date; expiry is reported as a warning, not a failure.

allow.reason: No release of the direct dependency resolves it. The advisory covers @graphql-tools/utils <=12.0.0 and a fixed 12.0.4 exists, but it reaches the Hono GraphQL template through @graphql-markdown/cli -> @graphql-markdown/types, whose latest release (1.16.1) pins @graphql-tools/utils to exactly 11.2.0. @graphql-markdown/cli 1.1.2 (latest) still depends on types ^1.16.1, so raising GRAPHQL_MARKDOWN does not help; npm's only suggestion is a downgrade to cli 0.4.3. It is a devDependency used by the optional docs:graphql script on the project's own schema file. Remove once @graphql-markdown/types depends on utils >=12.0.1.

No fixed version exists upstream. npm audit reports the vulnerable range as every published braces release, and 3.0.3 is the latest, so there is nothing to bump to. It reaches the res-x template through rescript-x -> fast-glob 3.3.3 -> micromatch 4.0.8 -> braces, each at its latest release. Impact is a stack-exhaustion denial of service on deeply nested glob patterns, which on this path come from the project's own build configuration.

No fixed version exists upstream. npm audit reports the vulnerable range as every published node-forge release, and 1.4.0 is the latest. It reaches the Expo template through expo -> @expo/cli -> node-forge (directly and via @expo/code-signing-certificates); npm's only suggestion is a downgrade to expo 44. Impact is lenient RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification inside the Expo CLI, a development-time tool.
